The State, being the custodian of public interest, is under a corresponding obligation to ensure that the exercise of statutory authority by its instrumentalities remains consistent with the principles of fairness, ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 33 of 38 transparency, reasonableness and the rule of law. Revenue administration occupies a position of particular importance in this constitutional framework, for the collection of taxes is indispensable to the discharge of the State's functions, while the persons and enterprises contributing to the national exchequer are equally entitled to the protection of law. The authority to assess and recover taxes, however extensive, is neither unregulated nor immune from constitutional scrutiny. It must be exercised strictly within the limits prescribed by law and in a manner which promotes certainty, predictability and confidence in public institutions. The State's legitimate interest in securing revenue cannot be pursued through procedures which impose unnecessary hardship upon taxpayers or deprive them of safeguards expressly provided by the legislature. Indeed, the efficacy of a fiscal system depends not merely upon its capacity to collect revenue, but also upon the fairness, consistency and integrity with which the relevant laws are administered. The constitutional foundation of this obligation is reflected, inter alia, in Article 25 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, which guarantees equality before law and equal protection of law. The guarantee is not confined to a formal declaration of equality; it also requires that statutory powers be exercised upon rational, consistent and non-arbitrary considerations. In this regard, reference may be made to the principles elucidated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1991 SCMR 1041, wherein the constitutional requirement of equal treatment was examined with reference to persons similarly situated. The principle assumes particular significance in administrative and fiscal proceedings, where the exercise of discretionary authority must remain subject to objective standards and the procedural protections established by law. Although every irregularity in administrative action does not necessarily constitute discrimination within the meaning of Article 25, an arbitrary or unjustified departure from the prescribed legal framework may attract constitutional scrutiny, particularly where it results in the denial of a meaningful opportunity to a person whose rights or liabilities are being determined. The constitutional guarantee of equality, read in conjunction with the right to due process under Article 10A, ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 34 of 38 thus reinforces the obligation of revenue authorities to administer the law fairly, consistently and without caprice.

39. The circumstances attending the assessment proceedings in the present case require consideration against these constitutional standards. The respondent was selected for audit under Section 177 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, in November 2020, whereas the subsequent proceedings culminated in an amended assessment order dated 28.06.2024. Notwithstanding the considerable period during which the matter remained pending before the Department, the show-cause notice under Section 122(9) was issued on 14.06.2024, immediately preceding the Eid-ul-Adha holidays falling between 17.06.2024 and 19.06.2024, with the respondent required to furnish its explanation by 24.06.2024. The practical effect of this sequence was that the respondent was left with only a few effective working days to address the matters raised in the notice, notwithstanding the substantial lapse of time preceding its issuance. Such circumstances are material to the assessment of procedural fairness. Where the Department has itself taken a prolonged period to advance proceedings, the subsequent compression of the taxpayer's opportunity to respond requires particularly careful scrutiny. The statutory power to issue a notice and prescribe a period for compliance must be exercised reasonably, having regard to the nature of the proposed additions, the complexity of the matters involved and the practical ability of the taxpayer to prepare an effective response. The requirement of providing an opportunity of hearing under Section 122(9) of the Ordinance is a substantive safeguard and not an empty procedural formality. Its object is to ensure that a taxpayer, before being subjected to an adverse amendment of assessment, is adequately informed of the proposed action and afforded a genuine opportunity to explain the relevant facts, produce supporting material and contest the legal basis of the proposed additions or disallowances. The mere issuance of a show-cause notice does not, by itself, establish compliance with this requirement. The opportunity must be real, reasonable and effective when assessed in the context of the surrounding circumstances. A notice which formally invites a response but allows ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 35 of 38 insufficient practical time for its preparation may fail to achieve the very purpose for which the statutory safeguard was enacted. This principle acquires added importance in proceedings involving intricate questions of accounting treatment, recognition of revenue, allocation of expenditure and the interpretation of fiscal provisions. The legitimacy of an assessment is therefore dependent not only upon the existence of statutory authority to make it, but also upon faithful observance of the procedure through which that authority is exercised.

40. The principles of natural justice and the constitutional guarantee of due process require that an affected person be afforded a fair and meaningful opportunity to meet the case advanced against him. These principles are not satisfied by a mechanical or superficial observance of procedural steps where the circumstances render participation ineffective in substance. In fiscal adjudication, the consequences of an adverse assessment may be substantial, and the obligation to observe procedural fairness must accordingly be approached with the seriousness which the nature of the proceedings demands. Administrative convenience, departmental delay or the desire to conclude proceedings expeditiously cannot, without lawful justification, displace the statutory right of hearing. Expediency is undoubtedly an important consideration in the administration of tax laws; nevertheless, it cannot be pursued at the expense of safeguards intended to secure the fairness and legality of the decision-making process. The requirements of reasonable opportunity and fair hearing must be understood as integral conditions of lawful adjudication rather than as technical obligations capable of being satisfied through formal compliance alone.

41. The principle of proportionality also informs the exercise of administrative discretion within the constitutional framework. An administrative measure must bear a reasonable relationship to the legitimate object sought to be achieved and must not impose an excessive or unjustified burden upon the person affected. In assessment proceedings, the objective of determining the correct tax liability is undoubtedly legitimate; nevertheless, ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 36 of 38 the procedure adopted to achieve that objective must remain proportionate to the nature and complexity of the inquiry. A prolonged period of departmental inaction followed by an exceptionally compressed opportunity for compliance may create an imbalance between the authority exercised by the Department and the procedural rights available to the taxpayer. Such an imbalance is particularly significant where the proposed assessment involves the examination of extensive financial records, contractual arrangements and questions of statutory interpretation. The requirement of reasonable opportunity operates as an essential restraint upon the exercise of fiscal powers and ensures that the pursuit of revenue remains compatible with the broader requirements of lawful administration.

42. The administration of tax laws must also be viewed in the wider context of the relationship between the State and those who contribute to its revenues. Taxpayers, whether individuals, entrepreneurs or corporate entities, play an indispensable role in sustaining public institutions, financing essential services, generating employment and supporting economic activity. The State is unquestionably entitled to recover every tax lawfully due; equally, taxpayers are entitled to expect that such authority will be exercised with fairness, courtesy, consistency and institutional responsibility. These are not competing considerations. A credible fiscal system is one in which lawful collection and procedural justice operate together. The relationship between revenue authorities and taxpayers should, therefore, remain regulatory in purpose, professional in character and conducive to voluntary compliance. The exercise of statutory powers must not assume an unnecessarily adversarial character, nor should the machinery of taxation become a source of avoidable uncertainty, harassment or disproportionate hardship for persons conducting legitimate business activities.

43. Commercial confidence and the effectiveness of revenue administration are closely connected with the predictability of governmental action. Businesses make financial commitments, undertake development projects and arrange their affairs on the legitimate expectation that ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 37 of 38 applicable laws will be administered consistently and that disputes concerning their liabilities will be determined through fair and transparent procedures. Arbitrary administrative conduct, unexplained delays and unreasonable procedural demands may undermine that confidence and generate avoidable litigation. The resulting consequences extend beyond the immediate dispute, as public resources are diverted towards the resolution of controversies which sound administration could have prevented. It is, therefore, incumbent upon revenue authorities to recognize that the efficient enforcement of fiscal laws requires more than the mechanical exercise of statutory powers. It calls for timely decision-making, careful consideration of the material placed on record, adherence to prescribed procedures and due regard for the dignity and legitimate interests of taxpayers. A system which secures compliance through confidence in its fairness is more consistent with the constitutional principles governing public administration than one which relies upon unnecessary coercion or procedural rigidity.

44. Before parting with the matter, it is appropriate to emphasize that revenue authorities discharge a public trust and are expected to exercise their powers with a corresponding sense of fairness, restraint and responsibility. The legitimate objective of maximizing lawful revenue collection must be pursued through procedures which inspire confidence in the impartiality and integrity of the fiscal system. Taxpayer facilitation should not remain confined to policy declarations or administrative assurances; it must find practical expression in reasonable timelines, transparent decision-making, respectful treatment and faithful compliance with statutory and constitutional safeguards. The dignity of the taxpayer and the authority of the State are not mutually exclusive considerations. On the contrary, the legitimacy of public institutions is strengthened when statutory powers are exercised in a manner that protects individual rights while securing the public interest. The effective administration of tax laws, the encouragement of lawful enterprise and the preservation of confidence in governmental institutions are complementary objectives, each contributing to the stability and prosperity of the State.

ITR 163 of 2025 | Page 38 of 38 45. For the foregoing reasons, having examined the questions referred to this Court in the light of the applicable statutory provisions, the principles governing recognition of income under Section 36 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, the limits of reference jurisdiction under Section 133, and the constitutional and statutory requirements of due process and fair hearing, we are of the considered view that the learned Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue committed no error of law in annulling the amended assessment order dated 28.06.2024. The proceedings culminating in the said order were materially affected by the denial of a reasonable and meaningful opportunity of hearing as contemplated under Section 122(9) of the Ordinance, and the Department has failed to establish any legally sustainable ground warranting interference with the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal. Consequently, the questions of law referred for our consideration are answered in the NEGATIVE, i.e., against the applicant-Department and in favor of the respondent. Resultantly, the instant Income Tax Reference is DISMISSED, and the impugned order of the learned Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue dated 18.12.2024 is maintained. The parties shall bear their own costs.
